title: Find the clients that will fail when Windows servers require NTLM signing (May 2027)
problem: The November 2026 Windows updates (KB5135557, CVE-2026-118737) make clients offer real NTLM signing by default, and in May 2027 Windows servers start rejecting NTLM clients that do not. You need the list of non-signing clients per server now, and a controlled way to enforce early once that list is empty.
steps: Install the Windows updates released on or after 10 November 2026 on clients and servers. Phase 1 changes what Windows clients offer; servers keep accepting unsigned clients and start auditing them.

On Windows Server 2019 and later, make sure NTLM enhanced auditing is on so the `Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational` log records event 4023 (server side) and 4022 (client side). Microsoft's NTLM logging guidance is at `aka.ms/ntlmlogandblock`.
Collect 4023 from file servers, application servers and domain controllers into your SIEM, or run the read-only snippet below per server.

Classify each event by the Negotiated Flags value, not by level (signed and unsigned are both logged as Warning): a connection is phase-2 ready when bit `0x10` (NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_SIGN) and bit `0x40000000` (KEY_EXCH) are set and Session Key Status is Present. `ALWAYS_SIGN` (`0x8000`) without `0x10` is the placeholder and will be rejected.

Group unsigned connections by client IP, client machine, user and server process, and give each group an owner: typical candidates are non-Windows SMB/HTTP clients, appliances, scanners and third-party authentication packages.

Fix the client (update, reconfigure, move to Kerberos) rather than planning an exception. If phase 1 itself breaks a specific client, `ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm=1` (REG_DWORD under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0`) stops that client offering signing — time-box it, it is a temporary compatibility switch.
When a server shows no unsigned non-anonymous connections over a representative period (include month-end jobs), set `ServerRequireNtlmSign=1` under the same key. No restart is needed.

Verify enforcement: a non-signing client now fails with `SEC_E_UNSUPPORTED_FUNCTION (0x80090302)` and the server logs 4023 with that status. Anonymous (null session) and guest connections are exempt by design.
pitfalls: Filtering on event level hides the problem: both good and bad connections are Warning.

The 4022/4023 events exist only on Windows Server 2019 and later with enhanced auditing; older servers give you no per-connection signing data, so prioritise them for upgrade or treat their clients as unknown.
This is NTLM-layer signing. It does not replace SMB signing, LDAP signing or LDAPS channel binding; check those separately.
Microsoft says the registry values may be removed in the future — do not build long-term exceptions on `ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm`.
done_when: Every server role has a list of clients that do not negotiate NTLM signing, each with an owner and a fix date before May 2027.
`ServerRequireNtlmSign=1` is set on servers whose 4023 data is clean, through GPO preferences or Intune, with the change recorded.
No client in the estate has `ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm=1` without a dated exception.

troubleshooting.cause: Server older than Windows Server 2019, or NTLM enhanced auditing not enabled
troubleshooting.fix: Check OS version and the NTLM auditing configuration from Microsoft's NTLM logging guidance; on older servers the events are not available.

troubleshooting.cause: The client does not offer NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_SIGN
troubleshooting.fix: Set `ServerRequireNtlmSign=0` on that server (immediate, no restart), confirm the client's 4023 entry shows the SIGN bit missing, fix the client, then re-enable.

troubleshooting.symptom: Connection to an old non-Windows server stopped working after the November update
troubleshooting.fix: Per KB5135557 a server that does not echo SIGN should make the client fall back; if it still fails, use `ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm=1` on the affected client only, with an end date.

rollback: Set `ServerRequireNtlmSign` back to `0` (the default) on the affected server; no restart is required.
Confirm with a fresh 4023 event that the previously rejected client authenticates again, then keep it on the remediation list.
